- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for 3–5 day horizons.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.2) or volatile, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply smoothing filter to dampen overshoots.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizons; if forecast deviates > 3σ from 30-day moving average, adjust toward historical mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns bullish after day 15, increase forecast by 2–4% for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak or trough.
